claims.statement: All backend implementations conform to a single uniform interface, BackendProtocol, an abstract base whose file operations default to NotImplementedError so a backend can implement any subset.

File operations (grep/glob/ls/read/write/edit/delete) live on the base BackendProtocol rather than only on the shell-capable subclass because StateBackend and StoreBackend have no process to exec into and implement grep/glob in pure Python with no execute at all.

Backend file tools are not thin wrappers around execute: they enforce literal-only (non-regex) matching, return structured GrepResult/GlobResult objects, support max_count truncation, and honor filesystem permission rules.
Backend operations return typed result dataclasses that carry either data or an error string instead of raising for expected failures.

ReadResult.__post_init__ enforces pagination invariants at construction: the start_line/end_line window is co-present and runs forward, total_lines is at least end_line, and next_offset must equal end_line so a backend cannot emit a resume offset that skips unshown lines.

Every sync backend method has an async twin; base async methods wrap the sync call with asyncio.to_thread, and agrep additionally bounds the wait with asyncio.wait_for(timeout=ASYNC_GREP_TIMEOUT) and forwards max_count only when the concrete grep accepts it, trimming afterward with _apply_grep_max_count.

delete is an optional backend operation; callers detect support via _supports_delete (comparing type(backend).delete against BackendProtocol.delete) rather than invoking it and triggering the NotImplementedError default.

The protocol module pins search timeout constants: DEFAULT_GREP_TIMEOUT is 15s, ASYNC_GREP_TIMEOUT is (2*15)+5 = 35s sized to cover ripgrep plus the Python fallback, and ASYNC_GLOB_TIMEOUT is 30s as the outer bound on a sandbox glob round-trip.

The outer ASYNC_GLOB_TIMEOUT exists because the remote sandbox glob script bounds only its own walk (TIME_BUDGET = 5.0s, MAX_EXPANSIONS = 1000, MAX_MATCHES = 10000), which does not cover interpreter startup, the round-trip, or record transfer, so without the outer bound a wedged sandbox would hang the caller.

Shell execution is a distinct capability added by SandboxBackendProtocol, which extends BackendProtocol with an id property and execute()/aexecute(); a backend that is not a SandboxBackendProtocol instance has no shell.

The middleware's supports_execution check gates whether the execute tool is available, and callers guard with execute_accepts_timeout before forwarding a timeout because older backend packages may predate the timeout keyword.

BaseSandbox is the reusable base for execution-capable backends: subclasses provide execute(), upload_files(), download_files(), and id, while inherited file operations are derived through execute() and transfer helpers.
Sandbox read() output is capped at MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES = 500*1024 bytes and appends TRUNCATION_MSG when the cap is hit.

StateBackend stores files in LangGraph agent state under the files key via Pregel internals (CONFIG_KEY_READ / CONFIG_KEY_SEND), reads with fresh=True for read-your-writes within a superstep, persists within a thread but not across threads, and requires a graph execution context or raises RuntimeError.

StateBackend is the default backend: FilesystemMiddleware uses StateBackend() when no backend is supplied and rejects raw callable factories (removed in deepagents 0.7) in favor of initialized backend instances.

StoreBackend adapts LangGraph's BaseStore for cross-thread persistent storage scoped by a caller-supplied NamespaceFactory, validating namespace components against a strict character set to prevent wildcard/glob injection, and resolving the store from the constructor or via get_store() at call time.

FilesystemBackend reads and writes real on-disk files under root_dir; with virtual_mode=True (default) it treats root_dir as a virtual root and blocks traversal, but this is a guardrail rather than sandboxing or process isolation.

LocalShellBackend extends both FilesystemBackend and SandboxBackendProtocol, adding unrestricted shell execution on the host with no isolation; virtual_mode restricts only file operations and never execute(), and its default execute timeout is DEFAULT_EXECUTE_TIMEOUT = 120 seconds.
LangSmithSandbox is a BaseSandbox subclass conforming to SandboxBackendProtocol that runs files and shell in an isolated LangSmith sandbox.
ContextHubBackend stores files persistently in a remote LangSmith Hub agent repository (with commit-based identifiers) and has no shell execution.

CompositeBackend routes file operations to different backends by path prefix using _route_for_path over routes pre-sorted longest-prefix-first, strips the matched prefix before delegating, falls back to the default backend for unmatched paths, and re-maps returned paths back under the route prefix.
CompositeBackend.ls('/') aggregates the default backend's entries plus a synthetic directory entry for each configured route prefix.

CompositeBackend aggregating operations surface the first backend error rather than masking it as partial success and OR the truncated flag, and the glob merge escalates truncation_reason so unreadable is never masked by a co-occurring budget truncation.

In CompositeBackend, execute is not path-routable: it always delegates to the default backend and raises NotImplementedError if that default is not a SandboxBackendProtocol; correspondingly supports_execution inspects the composite's default backend to decide shell availability.

FilesystemMiddleware resolves the chosen backend into a local resolved_backend before dispatching each file and shell tool, and refuses tool-level permissions on execution-capable backends unless all permission paths are scoped to composite routes.

ContextHubBackend batches accepted mutations behind a short worker window, presents pending and in-flight changes through a local read overlay, waits for each mutation's commit outcome, and refreshes/rematerializes mutations when Hub commit conflicts occur before retrying.

FilesystemMiddleware distinguishes configured model-visible tools from backend capability: its allowlist can omit tools entirely, read_file is mandatory in an explicit list, and listing execute or delete is a no-op when the backend does not support that operation.
Batch upload and download APIs return one typed response per input in input order, allowing a backend to report success or failure independently for each file.

StoreBackend overrides several asynchronous operations to use BaseStore's native async APIs, including aget, aput, abatch, and paginated asearch, rather than relying only on BackendProtocol thread wrappers.
LocalShellBackend starts commands with an empty environment unless env is supplied or inherit_env=True; inheritance copies os.environ before applying explicit environment overrides.
LangSmithSandbox opts into BaseSandbox capture-at-source execution-output offload and caches the async sandbox client per backend event loop, avoiding a fresh client connection pool for each command.

For root-wide CompositeBackend.grep, max_count is a global cap: each route receives only the remaining budget and the composite short-circuits later routes when it is exhausted, conservatively marking the result truncated.
A root-anchored CompositeBackend glob pattern skips routed backends unless it explicitly targets their prefix, so routed results cannot violate the protocol's search-root anchoring semantics.

CompositeBackend converts NotImplementedError from a routed backend's optional delete method into a DeleteResult error, while its upload and download paths batch inputs by backend and restore original response order and virtual paths.

FilesystemMiddleware can provide virtual-to-host path mappings only when a CompositeBackend uses LocalShellBackend as default and a route is a FilesystemBackend; store-backed routes and local filesystem routes paired with remote sandbox defaults have no shell-visible mapping.
